# simplevm_volume (Resource)

A SimpleVM block storage volume.

Creating, growing and deleting a volume are asynchronous: the provider polls SimpleVM until the volume is `available` (or gone, for delete); see `timeouts`. A volume that enters an error status fails the apply.

`name` and `size` change in place: a rename is immediate and a larger `size` extends the volume. Shrinking a volume is not possible in OpenStack, so a smaller `size` replaces the volume and destroys its data. Every other argument replaces the volume. Attach a volume to a VM with `simplevm_volume_attachment`.

The `extend` and `rename` request shapes are assumed from the SimpleVM wiki.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "simplevm_volume" "data" {
  name = "data"
  size = 50 # GiB; increasing it extends the volume, decreasing it replaces it
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the volume. Changing it renames the volume in place.
- `size` (Number) Size of the volume in GiB. Increasing it extends the volume in place. Shrinking a volume replaces it (data loss).

### Optional

- `project_id` (Number) ID of the SimpleVM project the volume belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id`. Changing it replaces the volume.
- `source_volume_id` (String) UUID of an existing volume to copy the new volume from. Changing it replaces the volume.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) Timeouts for long-running operations, as Go durations such as `30m` or `1h`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `volume_snapshot_id` (String) ID of a volume snapshot to create the new volume from. Changing it replaces the volume.

### Read-Only

- `device` (String) Device name inside the VM the volume is attached to, for example `/dev/vdb`; empty when detached.
- `id` (String) UUID of the volume in SimpleVM.
- `openstack_id` (String) OpenStack ID of the volume.
- `path` (String) Mount path of the volume as reported by SimpleVM; empty when not mounted.
- `status` (String) Current volume status as reported by SimpleVM, for example `available` or `in-use`.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Timeout for the create operation (default `10m`). A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) Timeout for the delete operation (default `10m`). A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) Timeout for the update operation (default `10m`). A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A volume is imported by its SimpleVM UUID.
terraform import simplevm_volume.data 3f2a9c4e-1b7d-4e8a-9c21-5d6f7a8b9c0d
```
